proposed_bcs_y_entries.notes: Smaller Pattern D sub-sub-dispatcher ABOVE FUN_004D8860. 272-byte switch handling 0x05 (init+set state byte 0x98), 0x0D (set state offsets 0xB0/0xB4), 0x10 (set state offset 0xF0), 0xD8/0xD9 directly, default branch falls through to FUN_004D8860. key_findings.title: FUN_004D8860 is a thin LuaActorImpl::vftable mapper
key_findings.summary: Every numbered opcode in FUN_004D8860's switch (23 of 24 cases) translates directly into a vtable trampoline call on the LuaActorImpl instance. The vtable slots used (5, 48-66, 82, 83, 89) span both the lower-half stateless/getter range and the upper-half Receiver-class range documented in BCS-Y-0092. No handler does Pattern D sub-dispatch internally

key_findings.title: 20-opcode fallthrough into single SendLog receiver
key_findings.summary: Cases 0x157-0x16A (20 opcodes) all dispatch to LuaActorImpl::vftable[63] = Network::SendLogReceiver. This is the largest fallthrough group in the entire FFXIV 1.x dispatcher graph documented so far. The wrapper passes param_1+0x14 (likely a log subcategory id) as the receiver's second arg, so the Receiver demultiplexes the 20 opcodes via that arg rather than via per-opcode dispatch

key_findings.title: Pattern D recursion is ABOVE FUN_004D8860, not below
key_findings.summary: docs/client-architecture.md, 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns' framed FUN_004D8860 as reachable from FUN_004DC690 cases, suggesting one tier of Pattern D below the central dispatcher. The actual reachability chain is two tiers: vtable[1] (Receiver.apply) -> FUN_0058CCA0 / FUN_0059CED0 (tier 2 sub-dispatcher) -> FUN_004D8860 (tier 3 sub-dispatcher). The parents FUN_0058CCA0 and FUN_0059CED0 themselves have ZERO direct instruction-level callers in Ghidra refs - they are vtable-stored Apply methods, consistent with the Receiver class pattern. This nests Pattern D one level deeper than client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns' describes

key_findings.title: 0x17B has dual dispatch paths
key_findings.summary: Opcode 0x17B (Network::ChangeShadowActorFlagReceiver, slot 89) is handled BOTH by FUN_004D8860 (event-family path, via FUN_005752B0) AND directly by FUN_004DC690's case 0x17B (per BCS-Y-0279 catalog). FUN_005752B0 is the unique handler with two callers in the entire chain. This proves that some opcodes have redundant dispatch wiring across the dispatcher hierarchy

key_findings.title: 0xCC is the only Pattern C case in FUN_004D8860
key_findings.summary: 23 of 24 cases are Pattern A (vtable trampoline). The single Pattern C case is 0xCC, which has two distinct handlers (FUN_00574780 primary, FUN_00575860 alt) selected by the entry-guard predicate FUN_00574AA0. Both handlers perform actor-impl swapping with RTTI checks (LuaActorImpl vs NullActorImpl) and Lua-state acquisition - this is the actor (re)initialization opcode and warrants special handling outside the vtable-mapper pattern

key_findings.title: 0x192 is state-gated
key_findings.summary: Only case in FUN_004D8860 with a non-trivial gate beyond *(this+0x80) != 0. Calls FUN_004B68A0 (returns *(this+0x20)) and only dispatches if the value is 4 OR 5. AddictLoginTimeKindReceiver is therefore active only in specific game phases - likely login/character-select transition states. The 0x192 = AddictLoginTimeKindReceiver association from BCS-Y-0092 corroborates this (login-time-tracking system is only relevant during login flow)

key_findings.title: BCS-Y-0362 findings already invalidated chain-key extraction for this dispatcher
key_findings.summary: BCS-Y-0362 proves that eight handlers produce no chain-key writes through the LuaActorImpl receiver path. The remaining cases use the same Pattern A vtable-trampoline shape, extending the negative to all 23 cases. FUN_004D8860 is therefore not a source of receiver_write_chain_key bindings.
